R4 JUDGEMENT (mine, not inherited): I AGREE WITH THE CRITIC. R4 reads "Interiors get their own bed, not the exterior bed at -12 dB." The main clause is positive and imperative - interiors GET a bed; the subordinate clause forbids one particular wrong bed. R1s null permission is explicitly per-LAYER inside a declared bed ("Every region declares all four layers, and a layer may be declared null"), not a licence for a whole cell to have no bed. The ARBITRATION note about silence being a design statement is scoped to a REGION ("silence in a dry region") and cites R1, i.e. layers. And RI-WLD08 §6 independently mandates ">=13 (one per region) + >=8 settlement beds + >=4 interior beds" - a positive count that silence cannot satisfy. Round 1s "interiors go silent and report suppressed" is therefore not permitted by the item. Building interior beds.

R4 JUDGEMENT, MADE AGAIN INDEPENDENTLY (successor, not inherited from the predecessor entry above). I AGREE WITH THE CRITIC, and I reach it by a route the critic did not use. R4s main clause is positive and imperative - "Interiors get their own bed" - and the subordinate clause rules out one particular wrong bed, it does not exhaust the space. But the decisive text is RI-AUD03s own "How we lose" list, which names the failure as: "Interiors are the exterior bed low-passed. R4. Cheap, universal, and it makes every building in the game feel like a tent. Nobody reports it because it is not WRONG, it is just NOTHING." An item that names "just nothing" as the loss cannot be satisfied by delivering literally nothing; silence is that failure taken to its limit, not an escape from it. R1s null permission is scoped to a LAYER inside a declared bed, and the ARBITRATION amendment ("silence in a dry region is a design statement") is scoped to a REGION and cites R1, i.e. layers. RI-WLD08 SEC6 independently sets a POSITIVE COUNT of >=4 interior beds, which an absence of beds cannot satisfy. Round 1s "interiors go silent and report suppressed" is not permitted. Building interior beds. NOT referring this as a seam question - the orchestrator asked me to refer only on disagreement, and I do not disagree.

DEFECT FOUND BY MY OWN INSTRUMENT, not in the verdict and not in the blind answers: THE NOISE LOOP SEAM CLICKS. makeNoiseBuffer generated exactly n samples and ambience.js set src.loop=true. Brown noise is an integrated random walk, so first and last samples are uncorrelated and wrapping STEPS - a click, once per 6 s buffer period, forever, in every region with a noise layer. SecA requires L1 "looped, GAPLESS"; it was not. Masked everywhere except the Stone Wastes (L1 brown at -16 dB, L2 declared null): with no bed to hide behind the seam read as a discrete event 10 dB over the floor at 3.12/9.12/15.12/21.12/27.12 s - exactly the 6.0 s period. The ONE region my tool reported transients for was reporting nothing but this. Fixed: buffers for loop are generated n+xf long and the tail cross-faded back over the head (0.25 s), plus DC removal before normalising.

SECOND DEFECT FROM MY OWN INSTRUMENT, and it is the one the loop-seam fix did NOT cover: SecA requires L1 "looped, gapless, >=30 s of material" and round 1 used SIX. Six seconds of brown noise is one random walk with two or three big slow excursions in it; looping it repeats those excursions on a 6 s cycle forever. Localised by muting: stone-wastes clicks arrived at 0.77 and 3.12 past EVERY buffer boundary (0.77, 3.12, 6.77, 9.12, 15.12, 21.12) and muting L1 removed all of them. LOOP_SECONDS is now 30, the items own number. Cost is generated memory (~11.5 MB per noise layer at 48 kHz), not shipped bytes.

AND A DEFECT IN MY OWN TOOL, found and corrected before any number was quoted from it: the first onset detector ran on the broadband mix and reported 98 onsets in the Stone Wastes and zero everywhere else - every one of the 98 false. That bed is a brown drone lowpassed at 70 Hz, and at 70 Hz a 10 ms frame is most of a cycle, so the 1.5x rise test fired on the carrier itself. It now detects on a 300 Hz-highpassed signal, which is what a discrete event actually is and what perceptual onset detectors do. Recorded because a tool that needed fixing before its first citation is exactly the thing RULES 4 exists for.

ITEM-LEVEL CONFLICT FOUND, and it is worth an amendment: THE B2 JUDGES CREST-FACTOR HEURISTIC AND RI-AUD03 SECA CANNOT BOTH BE SATISFIED. The judge gave ">20 dB crest = a bed carrying one-shots" as the detector-free corroboration of its zero-onset finding, and it is a sound heuristic about real recordings. But this builds filtered-noise beds measure ~12 dB of crest on their own, and clip crest is peak-over-RMS, so lifting it past 20 dB needs the events peak about 20 dB over the bed RMS. A short grain carries 6-10 dB of its own peak-to-RMS, leaving the events WINDOW level needing to sit near +10 dB rel bed. SecAs Level (rel. bed) column caps L3 at +2 and L4 at +4. Reaching the judges bar means putting the events ~8 dB OUTSIDE the band the item specifies. I did not chase the bar and I did not quietly drop it: O2 is now gated on a WITHIN-BED control (how much the events lift the crest of their OWN bed, same render with the event layers muted, >=3 dB) with the absolute figure and the judges 20 dB reported alongside so the tension stays visible.

ONSET DETECTOR WIDENED TO TWO TIMESCALES, and the change was made AFTER seeing an acceptance result, which I am recording plainly because that is the move that needs justifying. The 10 ms-only detector reported ZERO for marauders-coast and salt-hills. Their L3 signatures are rope_creak (attack 0.14 s) and dry_grass_gust (attack 0.45 s) - SEC Bs own words for those two regions - and a 10 ms rise test structurally cannot see a sound that takes half a second to arrive. The judges own phrasing was "not one bird, drip, gust or CREAK", so a gust is an event. Now: fast pass on 10 ms frames, slow pass on 100 ms frames, merged within 250 ms so one sound is counted once. What stops this being a fudge is --sabotage silent, which mutes the event layers and must still report zero.
